utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we have the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't want to pre-empt the Prosecutor, but I do have one matter. Yesterday a question was posed by Ms. Sinatra to Mr. Obrenovic with respect to equipment used to bury - or rebury - the individuals at Kravica. But in my interpretation, it looks like it was for the burial. On page 80 of yesterday's transcript, line 22, the question was posed: "Well, I don't refer to his testimony, but if Mr. Nikolic had said that the burial equipment that took care of the problems at the Kravica warehouse was strictly run by equipment from the Bratunac Brigade, that would make sense because Kravica is in the Bratunac zone of responsibility, isn't it?" And of course the answer was: "Perhaps." But -- and I didn't object yesterday because I wanted to be precise in making my record. And since I'm before professional Judges and not a jury, I didn't think it was necessary at the time to jump up at the time and make my speech. But I went through the record, and the first time that Mr. Nikolic refers to anything with respect to burials was when he was questioned by -- on direct examination by Mr. McCloskey. And that's where he indicates, and the relevant portions are on pages -- on page 1768. And he indicates that he attended a meeting, and I'll read it, from line 1: "I did so, and a meeting was organised at the Municipal Assembly building in Bratunac with the chief of the MUP ministry in Bratunac, Mr. -- And he says here Mr. Vespovic in attendance as well as president of the municipality, Ljubisa Simic, president of the Executive Board of Bratunac, Davidovic, and myself." And then he goes on: "They assumed the responsibility to talk to the presidents of those companies which actually owned the heavy equipment. That heavy equipment would be commandeered they said and used in the operation." Later on, again, the issue of burials or reburials was raised, and this time it was raised on cross-examination by Mr. Stojanovic. The relevant pages are 2281 to 2282. There is an exchange, but - and I don't wish to read it - but it is clear that Mr. Nikolic never indicated, never indicated that any heavy equipment of the Bratunac Brigade were used because -- and I don't think the Prosecutor has indicated that the Bratunac has such equipment. And if that is part of their case, they can present it. But at least with respect to Mr. Nikolic, he never testified. So the question that was posed to Mr. Obrenovic assumed facts which were not in evidence. And therefore, I just wanted to make clear for the record so later on it doesn't appear that I am not being due diligent in bringing these matters to the attention of the Court. And I certainly don't them to be used in the Court's reasoning when they make their findings of fact and conclusions of law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, thank you very much for your statement. But I believe that the Judges are professional Judges, and we could go into the transcript and find relevant parts on that issue. I believe that you are a very diligent lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to be on the safe side, Your Honour. I don't mean to be presumptuous. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, briefly, I believe Mr. Karnavas is correct. I do not recall Mr. Nikolic ever suggesting that the Bratunac Brigade was involved in the burials at this stage. And I think the problem he mentions highlights a significant problem, and that is the misstatement of facts, or the assumption of facts in the questions creates a record that will be impossible to make any sense of because none of us will be able to research every little misstatement. And I hate to jump up at every little misstatement. I was not precisely clear as Mr. Karnavas may not have been whether or not that was a misstatement. So I stayed down. But it also shows that that was a two-part question, whether Kravica was in the Bratunac Brigade zone and the other part, and so we get an answer of, you know, an affirmative answer. So doubly, we don't know what question the person is answering, and we don't -- we have a misstatement. So I don't want to object every time there's a misstatement or an assumption of facts, but this is a problem and it's a continuing problem. And I just wanted to add that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as far as the questioning goes of the witnesses right now, it is true that you are professional Judges and you will be able to look at the evidence and sort it out. But also we have a motion of for judgement of acquittal that will be filed at the end of the Prosecution's case. There will be final briefs filed, and if there are any loose ends that need to be attended to, we can cite to those problems and try to wrap them up in our own perspective at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, I believe all those issues are related to your questions. So could I suggest that whenever you quote whoever said in the transcript, would you please quote the paragraph, the lines in the transcript to avoid any misstatements in the future. I believe that Mr. Karnavas did that, which is very clear. You may read the relevant paragraph in the transcript to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will attempt to do that. And I have marked it in most parts of my questioning. But if I overlook one part of the transcript, I really don't want to take the Court's time up to find it. But I have tried to do that last night, to maintain that procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just briefly address another matter: And this relates to the statement Mr. Jokic gave to the OTP which I understand the Court has provisionally not allowed into evidence. And -- however, Ms. Sinatra, yesterday, as what I believe was a natural part of her cross-examination, challenged the veracity of the meeting between Mr. Jokic and Mr. Obrenovic when there was this brief exchange that was made. I think she challenged whether or not that indeed happened. And I believe, and I won't get into the detail, but in Mr. Jokic's statement, I believe there is information that would be very helpful to the Court on whether or not such a meeting occurred. And so I would be asking orally at this point for the Court to reconsider, on a limited basis, to consider the material Mr. Jokic provided the OTP that is relevant to this particular issue. If we could provide that to the Court for their consideration and admission into evidence as an admission against the interest of Mr. Jokic on the relevant topic that Ms. Sinatra has now challenged and put into issue, that is, this brief meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters where there was an exchange, I believe that would be helpful for the Court now that it is in issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, the Bench made a decision, I may say temporary decision, to not admit the statement of Mr. Jokic into the evidence at the very beginning of this trial. I think, you know, during the testimony of the first or second witness. We made this decision not because that this statement has not reached the criteria of the admission. What I am saying is that legally speaking, this statement is allowed to be admitted into the evidence. But on the other hand, we found that statement has very little probative value at that time so that we could not put much weight in that piece of the evidence when it is admitted. Of course, we made a decision at the very beginning of that trial, and things may change. And during the proceedings, I believe that parties could reintroduce those evidence which has not been admitted into the evidence at a future or at a later stage. We'll take into your proposal into the consideration and we'll make a decision at a later stage. Sometimes it's very difficult to make this kind of decision. It depends on the proceedings of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like us to provide you with some written material on that, or we can just go orally, whatever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think orally will be perfect to avoid the truckload of documents. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. McCloskey is asking the Trial Chamber to use -- would you like for me to stop for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, you may, please, continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. To use the statement in a form of attacking the credibility of Mr. Jokic. But the only time he is available to use his statement under well-established Laws of Evidence would be if Mr. Jokic testified, and he were going to use the statement to attack his credibility from his prior statement. He can't attack Mr. Obrenovic's credibility with the prior statement by Mr. Jokic when they were codefendants represented by co-counsel, the conflict is too clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but I think on line 18 of the transcript, there was a mistake this morning when Mr. McCloskey was speaking. He said about the brief meeting between Obrenovic and Jokic in the Bratunac Brigade. That's line 18 of the transcript. I think that there has been no reference to a meeting at the Bratunac Brigade, and I assume this is only because Mr. McCloskey misspoke. I think he was talking about the Zvornik Brigade. That is probably the meaning of his words, and we wish to have this corrected. We want the transcript to clearly reflect the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And Your Honour, just to clear up a matter yesterday, we had a misstatement in the presentation of the evidence yesterday that I would like the record to reflect that Mr. Krstan Simic will not and has not spoken to the Defence, and I had represented that he had spoken to Mr. Stojanovic and told him that he had given Mr. Obrenovic the tapes. It turns out that he had not spoken to Mr. Obrenovic -- I mean, to Mr. Stojanovic because he would not speak to the Defence team for Dragan Jokic. So I misspoke on that. Mr. Krstan Simic never spoke to Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take note of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry to keep you waiting outside, because we have some housekeeping matters to deal with. Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sinatra, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Good morning, Mr. Obrenovic. I do have one housekeeping matter which it is okay to have the witness in the courtroom. But in the statement that was provided to the Defence by -- between Dean Manning and Nenad Simic from 19 December 2001, it appears that there are nine pages missing in the English version. And if the Trial Chamber or everybody else in the courtroom could pull up the English version of Nenad Simic which we filed yesterday as D19/3, I would like in the English version to turn to page 18. And Dean manning says, as I said, 1524. And then on the next page, at the top, Dean Manning says: "It's 1628." During that time the B/C/S version continues with about an hour of testimony that has not been provided in the English statement. And therefore, we don't have those nine pages translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But if the Trial Chamber would allow me, I only have one line that we want to get out of this statement in the part that is in B/C/S. Could we provide Mr. Obrenovic with the B/C/S version, and I'll just ask him what Nenad Simic says on page 24 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, what's that problem? Did you provide the English translation of those nine pages to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is the first I've heard about this, Mr. President. We obviously are not perfect. I don't know if we did or not. We may have; we may have -- sometimes a few things are missed. It's a little difficult to hear at this hour that there is a mistake. And we can sort it out at the next break. And going into B/C/S and leaving us out in the English is potentially problematic. But also, I would just briefly mention, statements like this are generally used to refresh a witness's recollection or to impeach a witness. This habit of just reading people's statements and then commenting on it is not really proper. We could go on forever literally. There's so many statements to do that. So if there's a particular issue in the statement that needs to refresh the witness's recollection because his answer doesn't get to it, or if the answer on a particular topic is contradicted by something in a statement, then it's proper for impeachment. But this practice of just reading a statement and saying what do you comment on it appears that people are taking various statements that appear to support their case and reading it out. Both sides could go on endlessly like this with the various statements of people that will never come into Court. So yes, we will try to sort this problem out as soon as we possibly can. But I think it also highlights another potential problem that we're facing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that Ms. Sinatra is trying to impeach this witness statement. Maybe she did not express her very clear at this point. But I guess that you do not object to the using of the B/C/S for this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't object now. Let's see if it goes into areas. Maybe it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll see how far, how far we can go. Yes, Ms. Sinatra, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like the Court to notice that the pagination of the pages was perfect. It was just the missing of the time between the tapes, and until reviewing Mr. Stojanovic's statement last night, we don't notice the missing pages. But if I might show Mr. Obrenovic the B/C/S version of the statement of Nenad Simic. I'm sorry, page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, there has been no question. You can't impeach someone unless you have an answer to impeach. You can't refresh someone's recollection unless they have given an answer they don't remember. Just showing people things to comment is not proper adversarial procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I haven't seen, you know, that statement yet since this is the B/C/S. Maybe Ms. Sinatra at first is trying to reflect the memory of this witness. Then she will impeach this witness. I don't know. Let us see how far she can go.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, are you now on page 32 of Mr. Nenad Simic's statement in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found page 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Did you not state yesterday in your testimony that Nenad Simic was not the duty officer on the 15th, but that it was Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. So Mr. Obrenovic, this is Nenad Simic's statement. Could you read the line after he says "hvala, ako ste vi bili." Can you read that sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. "If you were the duty operations officer on the 15th, if you were the operations duty officer between the 15th and the 16th, then yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. So Mr. Simic says that he was the duty officer between the 15th and 16th, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I have nothing further from this statement, Your Honour. But I would like to have the Prosecutor to work with us and get the missing pages in English. Both of these documents in B/C/S and English have been introduced as D17, I believe. And we will try to provide the missing pages in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Sinatra, I don't see there's a conflict between the witness's statement and the paragraph you read out just now because I remember that the witness told us on the 15th to 16th, Mr. Nenad Simic was the duty officer. There's no contradiction between the two statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is contradiction between the two statements in that he also went to say, no, he believes that Drago Nikolic was the duty officer that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, he said that Mr. Dragan Jokic was the duty officer from the 14th to the 15th. So from the 15th to 16th is Nenad Simic. Right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, I heard him say that Drago Nikolic was duty officer on the 15th, and he has documents that reflect Nenad Simic as duty officer, and he has records that reflect Drago Nikolic as duty officers. So just to confirm from the statement of Nenad Simic, Nenad Simic says that he was duty officer on the 15th. I think it's an important piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obrenovic, for being our interpreter today. You do remember that Nenad Simic also stated that you were debriefed by him on the 15th of July in the morning, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember what you read yesterday from Nenad Simic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And on the 14th in the headquarters, there was a huge panic going on, wasn't there, on the 14th -- I mean on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th, as I said, I was not at the brigade headquarters physically. Therefore, I have no personal experience of that. But I assume that the few people who were actually there were probably in a state of panic or fear. On the 15th, also there were very few people there. When I came, there was hardly anyone to be found, with the exception of the conversation with Jokic and the group of people who were in the office. But this all happened very quickly, just as I had explained; that's if memory serves me. And we were in a state of panic, yes, indeed, including myself on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And on the 15th, the headquarters was in a state of panic, and people must have been busily trying to take care of all the procedures that went on with the requisition of soldiers and the combat proceedings. And you stated that no one else heard this discussion between you and Dragan Jokic. As I borrow from Mr. Karnavas, it was just four eyes and four ears. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already explained, on the way into the headquarters, the building of the headquarters, Vasic and I took the flight of stairs to the first floor. Jokic appeared on our right-hand side, and he called me over, and that's where we talked. I didn't see anyone else there. Vasic proceeded up the stairs towards the first floor, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: So are you saying that you met Mr. Jokic on the first floor or on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But Mr. Jokic's office is on the first floor, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you're referring to his office or to the office of the operations duty officer. But whichever of the two you mean, both are located on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: So there was really no need for Mr. Jokic to be on the ground floor, was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what his needs were. I only told you when I saw him. He was coming from the corridor on my right. What he was doing there, I really don't know. I don't know what his purpose was, but he needed to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your statement today is you met Mr. Jokic on the first floor, and you talked to him somewhere near the duty officer's room. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that. I said that I was stopped by Jokic to have a word with him, and that was on the ground floor. As I was entering the building, he called me from the right-hand side corridor. Again, I repeat, it was on the ground floor, not on the first floor, and it was to my right, in the corridor to my right, and I believe that is exactly what I said a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But there really is no reason for Mr. Jokic to be on the ground floor, is there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know how to answer your question. I told you where I saw him. Why he was there at that moment, he never told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And he --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him explaining to me his reasons for being there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And when you met Mr. Jokic with Mr. Vasic, Mr. Vasic decided to go on up the stairs at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That is a deliberate misstatement of the evidence, which is just improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, as I instructed you not long ago that if you want to quote whatever the witness said, you have to quote the exact words in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm questioning him from his own memory, not from his testimony before. He says he's remembering this right now, and I'm asking him if he met Mr. Jokic and Mr. Vasic on the ground floor, and then he stated that Mr. Vasic went up the stairway. If he knows from his own memory without having to refer to a transcript, I'm asking for his own personal memory on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't want to belabour the point, Your Honour, but Mr. Obrenovic has clearly said numerous times that as he was coming in and going up the stairs, Jokic came in from one direction and Vasic continued. He has never said or implied that there was a meeting between Vasic, himself, and Mr. Jokic. That was implicit and suggested directly in her question to him. It's a deliberate misstatement designed to provoke the witness or confuse the evidence or whatever. But it's absolutely improper, and it's -- it's improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, since you provided us with the model, and I think we should make the best use of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you ask the witness to point where they met with Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, I would love to do that. If we could get the usher please to help us with the model and take it down to the ground floor, then we can find exactly where Mr. Obrenovic met with Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, could you please point with the pointer to somewhere in the ground floor that you met with Mr. Jokic as you and Mr. -- Colonel Vasic were coming into the building.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two of us entered here. This I believe, is the main entrance to the building. If my memory serves me, the staircase is here. So immediately from the entrance, I walked across there area here, and then we started climbing the stairs. And if my memory serves me well, the staircase is straight in front of the entrance. And as the two of us started climbing the stairs, from the ground floor to the first floor, that is, from this part here on the right-hand side, Major Jokic came, and he said "a moment, please." He called me. I made a few steps back, and here in this corner we exchanged a few words, the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And at that point on the first floor, on the ground floor where he met, where was Colonel Vasic at that point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already told you, we already climbed a few steps. I made a few steps back. Colonel Vasic did not go back. He continued climbing. And when I finished my conversation, I climbed the stairs, and that's where Colonel Vasic was waiting for me, on the landing which separates the offices from the other part of that corridor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But Colonel Vasic could have heard Mr. Jokic calling you, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of us were standing close to each other. If I heard him, I suppose he could hear him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All right. I'd like to go on to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'd like to go on to clear up D17/3, which was the statement by Nada Stojanovic yesterday. And in reviewing the complete statement, Bruce Bursik does not ask about a date certain. But to corroborate the testimony of Ms. Stojanovic, I do have the military police roster for that day, for July 14th. And on that roster, it states that Nada Stojanovic on the 14th went out to Orahovac, and it's the only corroborating evidence we have. It was provided to us by Mr. Butler through the OTP expert. And I'd like to know if I could introduce this as corroborating evidence that Ms. Stojanovic made the statement about meeting Mr. Obrenovic at headquarters on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you could introduce it. But that piece of document should be tested.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Should I have the witness take a look at it? Because I don't know that he's familiar with the military police logs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: May we provided a copy of this document to Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps it could simplify matters, Your Honour. We can stipulate that the police log is genuine. We did get it in a search warrant. It is mentioned in Mr. Butler's report. It does indicate that she was at Orahovac on the 14th. And it's a clear part of the evidence here. So perhaps we can save time. My objection was she keeps using this term "the 14th." That was not part of the record of Bruce Bursik's.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The day that she was at Orahovac is the day that she said she saw Mr. Obrenovic. That's fine. That perhaps solves the problem, and we can go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us see what kind of question Ms. Sinatra was going to ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, if there's no objections from Mr. McCloskey stating that this is corroborating evidence, he accepts it, that Nada Stojanovic went to Orahovac on the 14th, then I think we have corroborating evidence that's uncontested to support the fact that she went to Orahovac on the 14th. She returned to headquarters and saw Dragan Obrenovic. I can ask him more questions about it, like does he recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I have no objection to this material being used for impeachment purposes. And as such, that's fine. Material that's used for impeachment purposes is generally not to be used as substantive evidence of fact and is generally not, therefore, admissible. Of course this will be admissible -- is part of the record. But we need some structure here, otherwise this will become complete chaos with all these documents floating around being used substantively when they're actually being used for impeachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think I have already allowed Ms. Sinatra to use this document and ask some questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But frankly speaking, I fail to see how important this document this is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Obrenovic states emphatically, absolutely no that he was not at headquarters on the 14th. Ms. Stojanovic states that she ran into Obrenovic at the headquarters on the evening of the 14th. So I think it's clear for impeachment purposes to get a picture of where he was located during these days, the 13th, 14th, and 15th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this list of the people present in the police on the particular day? I know what it is. I know -- I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I think it's a military police roster for who was present and where they went that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And can you please look at the fourth person down, Nada Stojanovic. And then I think you travel over to the 14th, and the marking there is a T, which means "terrain," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nada Stojanovic, on the 12th, on the 13th, and on the 14th, T, which means terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And does that represent that she was in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this here, if you look at only this paper, I can see T. But this does not suffice to tell me that she was in Orahovac. T can mean anything. But from other sources, we know that she, indeed, was in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also have a summary from Mr. Butler's report stating where everybody was located at a certain time. If I can have the assistance to find it real quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps we can clear this matter up, Your Honour. On the original of this log, and we have an expert report that counsel has, you can see that the T has been erased. And underneath it is an O. And then on the back of the document, there are several letters indicating T means terrain, and then it's O means Orahovac. And this is what Mr. Butler and others have based their opinion on, that the people with the O next to their name were at Orahovac. So it gets deeply into the evidence. But this is basically where she is, I think, trying to suggest, just if that can be of some help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, okay, Your Honour, it appears that we may have to verify this information at another time, but I would like to have that opportunity, to provide the Court with the Butler report summary of Mrs. Stojanovic being at Orahovac on the 14th. But we'll have to pass for right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, sorry to interrupt, I was wondering if you could identify this particular document for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I believe this will be D29/3, or D28/3? And it's military police --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be D27/3 in my list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay, D27/3. It is the military police roster for the month of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have -- from this list just furnished to us, we have another D27/3. That is OTP interview with Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So it will be D29/3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. D27 is the interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, if it will save some time, the Prosecution is willing to stipulate that according to that document, that document indicates with other documents that I just told the Court about, that Nada Stojanovic was at Orahovac on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So there's no dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will accept that stipulation. And I just hope that the Court remembers the testimony - I don't need to refresh his memory with the testimony at this point - and I would just like to go on to the next topic if the Court -- I mean if the Prosecution stipulates that it was on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Okay, Your Honour, I'm going to bring up what I think is marked D27/3. Is it the statement by Mr. Obrenovic from 2 April 2000?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that according to list, it's the June 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm looking for the marking for the 2nd of April 2000. And if there isn't one, I guess this would be D28. It's the statement from April 2nd, 2000.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be D28/3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. With the usher's assistance, to provide a copy of the B/C/S to Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could, again, she make it clear what we're referring to if we're not going to be provided copies, could we at least research our own records.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to be looking at page 62, line 13 through 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you please repeat which document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, it is now marked D28/3, page 62, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Through 24. And after reading the part out of the statement, Your Honour, there will be a question following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that, Your Honour. That is improper. There needs to be a question first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: You stated that Mr. Jokic met you in the hallway on the morning of the 16th and debriefed you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th? No, no, on the 16th, I was in Baljkovice, and nobody came there, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Sorry. It was on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th, yes, I showed it to you a little while ago on the model.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. And in your statement that you gave in the year 2000, you stated that that was on the 15th at 9.00 in the morning upon deployment on the heights in the area, I got my vehicle and hurried to Zvornik. When we searched the part of the route of Brezik where all these curves we found two trails where the main body of the 28th division went --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please read slowly. The document is not on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: It concerns two tracks, actually 2 metres wide --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me it, greatly assists the interpreters to have the document on the ELMO as well as the public if she is going to read. But again, what the relevance of all this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sure, sure, we'll put that English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologise. Did you mention page 63?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I mentioned page 62 in English.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page is that in the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: "And on the road, when I was on the road, I asked through the radio centre to find someone from the MUP, Colonel Vasic or someone, sometime after 9.00. I got to the barrack most probably around 9.30. And at the entrance of the barracks, I met with Colonel Vasic who was the head of MUP in Zvornik." And that's where you stop. You go on to the office. I would like to ask you, is there a reason why you never mentioned Dragan Jokic meeting you on the 15th in your 2000 statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a reason, and I explained the reason yesterday. In the statement that I gave in April 2000, I did not mention any of the incriminating facts. I didn't mention this conversation; I didn't mention the telephone conversation which took place two days before that; I didn't mention anything concerning the execution of prisoners of war. That's why I skipped this particular conversation that you're now asking me about. That was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: You didn't mention anything because you were trying to tell your own story, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you. At that time, I didn't speak of anything that had to do with the execution of prisoners of war. I just omitted that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And by omitting that, you gave a false statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'd like to go to D18/3, which is the statement of Mico Gavric, and I believe we have the correct statement today. And I'll be referring in the English version to page 55, line 13. In the B/C/S version, do you know what the reference is? Page 50 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, you stated that you never went to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters on the 14th. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But Mico Gavric, on the 28th of November, 2001, says: "When you went to Zvornik on the 14th, did you see any captured Muslims there?" Mico Gavric: "They were no there, because we arrived at the reception room, and we reported, and we arrived where we were just given a room where I could go with my soldiers to take a rest and wait further orders." Dean Manning: "Did you see any Zvornik Brigade officers?" Mico Gavric: "Obrenovic was there." Dean Manning: "What time during the night did you see Obrenovic? What time during the day did you see Obrenovic?" Mico Gavric: "During the night." Dean Manning: "What time?" "Between 1.00 and 1.30 in the morning." Now, Mico Gavric has seen you in the brigade headquarters on the 14th; hasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the 14th, I was not in the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade. Mico Gavric must have made a mistake. I don't know why. Three days ago, Mr. Karnavas showed me three or so documents, one from Zvornik, and two from Colonel Blagojevic, which said that at that time, none of the units of the Bratunac Brigade were in Zvornik. He made a mistake. I don't know why he made it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But you can confirm that Mico Gavric says that he saw you at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters on the 14th. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Ms. Sinatra, I can't confirm that he saw me because he didn't because I wasn't there. It was an error on his part, so I can't confirm this error.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: My question was, but you can confirm that Mico Gavric says in his statement that he saw you there, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a different story. In this statement, Mico Gavric claims he saw me, but again, I say he could not see me because I simply wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now, you stated on your direct that you didn't know anything about the CZ. We have another document which has not been marked for identification yet, so I think it will be D29/3.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D30/3, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, that's a misstatement of the facts as stated. It was a rather more complicated issue yesterday on that point. I don't -- It's not what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the evidence will speak for itself. I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us see that document first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, this is a document from the Official Gazette of the Republic of Srpska, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And it's dated Tuesday, the 29th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And it's a directive that was issued by the government of Republic of Srpska.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, legal act on the organising and functioning of civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And there is an excerpt, chapter 11, part 10, article 21, dealing with asanacija. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the asanacija is -- do you recognise this document from the Republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But you knew -- you were aware of it, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it was submitted to us by the Office of the Prosecutor, I've probably seen it in that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, it was not submitted by the Office of the Prosecutor. It's being submitted by the Defence, but it came from the Republic of Srpska. And may I read to you the purpose from the civilian protection organisation when it comes to asanacija. And then I'll ask you to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in prison on the 29th of 2002, and I only had occasion to read what was given to me by my Defence counsel or the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But the Official Gazette is the official documents filed each day in the Republic of Srpska that becomes law, doesn't it? "On asanacija, with the view of preventing diseases, epidemics and other consequences of war actions, natural disasters, technical, technological, and ecological accidents, as well as other damages in time of war and peace, asanacija shall be organised and conducted by way of removing and burying corpses of perished animals and removing waste and other matters which might be hazardous to lives and health of people. "In the organising and conducting of asanacija, public utilities, civil engineering, construction, transportation, healthcare, and veterinarian companies, enterprises, and organisations are engaged as well as scientific and expert institutions, and as needed, the units of civilian protection." This document -- this civilian protection organisation is something totally separate from the military, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the Republic of Srpska has provided for the asanacija to be maintained by the civilian protective organisation, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We talked about Mr. Jokic wearing two hats, that of chief of engineering and that of the duty officer, on the 14th and the morning of the 15th. It was his turn to rotate in as a brigade operational duty officer, and his permanent position was that of chief of engineering, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic establishment-wise held the post of chief of engineers, with the Zvornik Brigade, with the staff of the Zvornik Brigade. And he was the operations duty officer pursuant to an order by the commander following a roster of duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the roster of duty officers is supplied for a seven- to ten-day period. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say precisely. It may have been like that. Maybe for 15 days, for a period of 15 days. Usually there would be one month, and then it would be updated whenever necessary. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But when it became your turn to rotate in, it was your turn to rotate in for that 24-hour period. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already explained, the brigade commander and the chief of staff, that's myself, were not duty officers at the brigade. Other officers were pursuant to a decision of the brigade commander, but I was not on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Who drafted the roster for the duty officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The roster was drawn up pursuant to an order of the commander, of the brigade commander, on organising duty, or rather operations duty. So the operations officer would draft a proposal, and then the commander would define -- further refine the proposal as to who could be on duty and who couldn't. And there was a group of officers - this was generally known - a group of 15 officers or so pursuant to this order, and the list contained therein one of the operations officers would schedule these officers according to the days for specific days of the week and what the duties of each of the individuals on duty would be, or of the units. There was a rule that no one should be on duty more than four times a month, that everyone should have the same number of hours of being on duty over a weekend, so there was an operations officer who would draw up the schedule, and the commander would then take final decisions as to who specifically would be on duty on a certain day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the commander you're referring to is Colonel -- Commander Pandurevic. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: We discussed the other day that there was friction between Drago Nikolic and Commander Pandurevic because Drago Nikolic didn't feel like he should have to sit in as duty officer. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point, yes, there was tension or friction, as you say. Not only because of that particular duty, but also because of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: What were the other frictions between Drago Nikolic and Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander tried to prevent Drago Nikolic from using the brigade stamp above his own signature. He tried to prevent him from using the code or the call signal without the commander's approval to send his reports like that. He wanted absolute control, just to put it in simple terms, over Drago Nikolic as over anyone else. Also as concerns the duty roster, for example.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And Drago Nikolic would send communications without the approval of the Commander Pandurevic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the rules governing the work of the security organ in the JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, which was then taken over by the VRS, and then pursuant to a directive which Mr. Karnavas disclosed before the Court, some possibilities were open for the security organ. Therefore, Lieutenant-Colonel Drago Nikolic was free to send his reports to Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic without necessarily informing the commander about their contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. The engineering company was under the command of Dragan Jevtic. He was the commander, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Jevtic was the commander of the engineering -- engineers company. In the VRS, that is the lowest rank which is referred to as commander, the battalion commander. And Jevtic was precisely that. He was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to refer now to what has been marked for identification purposes as D26.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just from a technical standpoint, is it possible for me to plug my headphone in over here so I can reach over to the desk? I'm not sure if there's a place for it to plug in here. I was just wondering. I'll try it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm afraid we have to ask the technicians about that. I hope some day we could have wireless microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Give me a little more leash here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, you have before you the combat rules for the engineering company platoon. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to read it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Now, I would like to have you tell us what the duties are of the engineering department. This is the description of what the company commander does. Dragan Jevtic. If you could tell us what basically the duties of the company commander are. Could you tell us from reading this document what the basic duties are of the company commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the engineers company, well, to be quite honest, I really don't know all of the duties for all the companies that we had across our units. I can only try to recall what they were. But in our brigade, we had -- well, the purpose was not for every rule to be learned by heart. I didn't know every single rule by heart, if that's what you mean. If I needed something, I would go to the rules and look for it. I'd refresh my memory and prepare myself for work. I can't know these things by heart, the duties of the commander of an engineers company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Would you say that the commander of a company such as the engineering department, that he organises the company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means, the commander of the engineering company would be subjected to a certain set of rules, as any other commander. He commands the engineers company. He knows the structure. He's familiar with the equipment and weapons at their disposal. He must be familiar with his soldiers. He must be familiar with the rules of his particular branch, and all these other general duties. Since we have the rules here before us, I think we just best go through them and maybe read them because they state very clearly what the duties are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: He receives tasks verbally on site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you're asking me how tasks are assigned. If that's what you're asking me, speaking about the commander, he can receive an assignment in a written or oral manner. That's the mode of reception. The other thing you need to look at is where he receives instructions or tasks. I could tell you a lot of things about these possibilities if you're interested in. I'm not sure if you want to go that far.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: We probably don't want to go that far, but thank you, Mr. Obrenovic. I'd just like to get out paragraph 26 which says that "along with the order for carrying out the task, the company platoon commander usually receives technical documentation. Absence of technical documentation cannot be the reason for nonfulfilment of the task..." So even if he doesn't get recommendations or proposals from the chief of engineering, the company commander still has to proceed with the tasks. Isn't that what that's saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. I appreciate that. The next document we have is Document D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, I think you are coming to another document. It's time for the break. Shall we break here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I would like to go back to what's marked for identification purposes as D26. I think it might be in front of you. Do you still have D26 in front of you? It's the combat rules for the engineering company. Okay, thank you. And I just forgot to cover Rule 25, paragraph 25. Isn't it true that the company is under the command of a company commander, and the platoon is under the command of a platoon commander? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes, that's correct. That's what the rule states. However, when Mr. McCloskey was examining me, I explained all the possible variants in relation to these rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Talking about exceptional circumstances. But as a general rule, the procedure is the company is under the command of the company commander, and the platoon is under the command of a platoon commander, right, under normal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under normal circumstances, yes. And it is the right of a brigade commander to define what these exceptional circumstances, as you say, are and to put his idea into practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the company commander and the platoon commander receive their tasks from the commander of the unit to which the company and platoon organisationally belong. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the chain of command, the company commander, in this case the commander of the engineers company would have received his orders from the brigade commander. That's one variant. The other variant is he receives his orders through the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When Dragan Jokic took over as duty officer, he relinquishes his duties at the engineer company, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And he would never act as the commander of that company, would he? The chief of engineering could never act as the commander of the engineering department, would he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I'm getting a correct interpretation. These are military concepts. I think there has been some confusion with departments and chiefs. If I understand this correctly, if I understand your question, chief of engineers is not the same duty as the commander of the engineers company. These are two distinct positions. There is a possibility under certain circumstances for the brigade commander to make a decision to give the chief of engineers the right to command the engineers company. But this might be pursuant to a specific decision by the brigade commander in a given -- under a given set of circumstances. But if the chief goes elsewhere, then he is on a different mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And if Captain Jevtic was not -- if he was absent as the commander of the engineering company, then the deputy commander of the engineering company takes over that command, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow just a small correction, Jevtic was not a captain. He was a private, but he was also the company commander. And you are right; in the absence of the company commander, which in this case was Mr. Jevtic, then automatically the duty would have been assumed by the deputy commander of the company who is also the assistant commander for moral guidance in that same company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And that deputy commander who assumed the command position in the engineering company, when Dragan Jevtic went to the field, was Slavko Bogicevic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And then if Slavko Bogicevic is absent, then it went to Lazarevic, I believe is his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, it's hard for me to say. But in principle, if the company commander is not there, then his deputy stands in. If there's no deputy, then there is the commander of the 1st platoon. Damjan Lazarevic was part of the company and he was one of the platoon commanders. I can't remember if it was the first platoon specifically or not, but he may have been the commander of the 1st platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And Slavko Bogicevic was present in the engineering company on the 14th of July, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, he was present, but my information is based on these statements that you read because I wasn't -- well, when I said that on the 13th, on the afternoon of the 13th, I was in the engineers -- at the engineers company, he was there. As to where he may have gone later on, I really can't say. However, on the 13th, when I had taken Jevtic there - Bogicevic was there, too, and Jokic was there, too at the engineers company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But Bogicevic assumed the position of deputy commander, and Mr. Jokic went on to assume the position of duty officer, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was an automatic thing. This was not assumption of position like you said. This was implicit. If a commander gets killed, he's automatically replaced by his deputy to keep the chain of command intact. And continues. Now, this is a different problem you're posing there in your question. The operations duty officer, we said when the shifts would change, in the morning generally speaking between 8.00 and 9.00 in the morning. Sometimes it was a bit later for different reasons, but mostly it was between 8.00 and 9.00 in the morning throughout that period. And on the 14th, as we said, Jokic was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I was going to refer to your April 2003 interview which is marked as D28/3. On page 27, and we just discussed the normal chain of command like in the engineering department. But in the year 2000 in your testimony, on page 27, you said: "There is a possibility of someone coming from the superior command when this chain of command can be broken. So on his decision, any link in the chain of command can be eliminated." I believe you were talking about at that point if someone came from main staff, then the normal chain of command we just went over for the engineering department could be broken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Counsel has mentioned two different interviews, and the same question. And the 2000 and 2003, and I'm not sure which one it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I meant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think Ms. Sinatra made a mistake in presenting the document. I believe it's the interview in April 2000, instead of 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And I'm sorry. It was April 2nd, 2000. That's on page 27.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: So this is an extraordinary situation that would break the normal chain of command, wouldn't it, as you stated in your interview?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, do you have that document at your hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honours. I don't. I have the one dated the 4th of June, 2003. Yes, I've just received it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S version, I believe it's page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In the B/C/S version, I believe it is on page -- and the winner is... There's no page number, he said. In the English version, it's page 27. And I don't have a page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But you remember stating that, that there is a possibility for someone coming from the superior command, for this chain of command to be broken. So on his decision any link in the chain of command could be broken. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably said. There is such a possibility indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. We can go on. I'd like to go to page 30 of the English version. And I would like to have the coordinations with the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I believe that the Defence team is telling me that the OTP didn't number the B/C/S version of the statement, but I can't see that it couldn't be numbered. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there any ERN numbers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Let us have the ERN number that coordinates with... I'm on page 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Krstan Simic clears up some of the things that you were talking about during your interview with the OTP in 2000. And he explains the ERN number on the English version is 01103595. The crisis situation: "In the crisis situation, does the responsibility of the commander increase to control the crisis situation?" And your answer was: "The commander's responsibility is commander's responsibility. It exists always. It always exists, and of course in critical situations, the outcome of the struggle depends on the correctness of decisions if talking in principle." Now, that statement also applies to the commander of the engineering department, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applies to every commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Let me ask you, when you said that Dragan Jevtic was the acting commander of the engineering company, by using the term "acting," you just mean that he is the commander but he doesn't have the appropriate military training or experience to hold that position? So he can't actually become the commander; he's just called the acting commander because of his lack of qualifications?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe that was the reason why the commander decided that. In any case, Jevtic did not have a rank. He did not complete his military education. He was an engineer, an architect. There was not enough officers at the time, and that may have been the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. I would like now to refer to what's been marked as D23/3. I believe it's from the Federal Secretariat of National Defence, rules on utilising of the engineering department. It says on the exhibit list 1983, but in actuality, that was a mistake. It's 1988. Mr. Obrenovic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this while I worked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: While you were in command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even before that, when I was doing my military education, and later on, and I also saw it when I was the commander. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And this incorporates all the duties and work of the engineering organ on preparation and organising engineering security. Paragraph 40, duties of the engineering organ are as follows. Can you briefly summarise by looking at this, and since you're familiar with the document, what the duties of the engineering organ are?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, this is the rule on the utilisation of engineers. And an engineering organ in this specific case is the chief of engineers. This is a regulation, and it speaks in general terms. This document here lists his duties in Article 40. In principle, he is responsible for the training of his men. Then he also keeps abreast of the issues pertaining to his area of responsibility. He cooperates with the intelligence organ on matters that have to do with engineers and issues; proposes to the commander the most appropriate way of organising and utilisation of engineers in order to complete a certain task; monitors the completion of that task, and so on and so forth. Maybe the best thing for me to do would be to read verbatim what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, if you'd like to, sure, we would like to read that in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document speaks for itself. It's not relevant to read it. It doesn't provide anything for the Court. That is an undue consumption of time. There's no reason to read a that's already before us. We'll stipulate this document into evidence if there's an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we have this document already, Ms. Sinatra. If you have a question, you may put it directly to this witness. And later on, if there's a need for reference to this document, we could come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I will ask him some questions from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, the engineering organ is an expert organ that recommends things to the commander and the deputy commander, right? Or the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And in so, it says he "consults with the organs of the command, makes recommendations to the organs of the command." And some of the areas that he is involved with are anti-armour units, discussing, you know, the plan to use anti-armour, and anti-descent combat activities. He participants in making crypto protection documents, is that right, for the engineering units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: He controls the tasks issued to subordinate engineering units, and monitors the effectiveness of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If there was something specific, I wouldn't object, but counsel just appears to be reading the document now. So I don't -- this is again, unduly time-wasting. If there's a specific question, I don't think Mr. Obrenovic disagrees with this document in any way. And we would all -- a question is perfectly appropriate on any of these topics, but this is just a recitation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, if you have some doubts, and if you want to impeach this witness's testimony, you may put your question directly which means that if you have any questions to put to this witness, just put it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not going to impeach this witness with this document, but I need him to confirm the duties of the engineering organ. Since he is a military expert, he has had all the training, and these are very important to the Defence of Mr. Jokic as to what he had authority to do. The indictment alleges that he could do anything from calling in the militia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's just not true. Mr. Obrenovic clearly explained the duties of the engineering officer, very much like is in this document, on direct. He has redone it on cross, and now he is not disagreeing with this document. I have no problem with a question of this document or a particular duty. But my problem is the mere recitation of the document is an unduly waste of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there is a point there; that is, we want to know the function of Mr. Jokic at that time. If you have some questions in this aspect, just put it directly to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, the truth is that as chief of engineering, you are someone who advises and proposes to the commanders of the brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't know whether the interpretation was good. Did you just say that I was the chief of engineering? That's the interpretation I'm getting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The chief of engineering is an expert organ that proposes and advises the commander and the deputy commander of the brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the commander or the deputy commander makes his decisions based upon the information given him by the chief of engineering. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I need to explain this. I need to clarify this. I've already said that the general principle in the army was the unity of command. It could not be either the commander or the deputy. When the commander is there, then it is the commander. When he is not there, then the duties are assumed by his deputy. That's one thing. And the second thing, the thing that you put to me in your question, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So he proposes and advises the commander, whoever that might be at the time. Is that right? And then the commander makes a decision and issues an order based upon that information that was given to him by the expert. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A commander makes an assessment and decides whether to accept this opinion or not, or change things. And then he makes a decision; that is, issues an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And then that order is transferred to the commander of the engineering company who is to implement the order. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also possible. But it is also possible that the commander will make a decision and can issue a direct order to the commander of the engineers, or the chief of engineers. And he can also tell the chief of engineers to implement the thing that he previously proposed. It's up to the commander to decide one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But the chief of engineers does not issue the orders; the commander issues the orders. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander issues orders. And if he authorises the chief of engineers, and not only the chief of engineers, but also the chief of communications, for example, then on behalf of the commander, this particular chief can exercise this authority and issue orders on behalf of the commander if this has been granted by the commander by way of an explicit order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I think we have a miscommunication here at this point, but to me, and what I'm trying to say, is the chief of engineer receives the order from the commander. Now, the chief of engineer cannot issue orders; he can only implement the orders given by the commander. Is that correct? He may issue tasks but not orders.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can you issue tasks and not orders? Okay, let's agree that that is the case. Let's not go into details of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the person who is chief of engineering has to stay updated on all of the latest technical, engineering, continuing legal education so that he can advise the commander properly. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is implied that one of the duties of the chief of engineers is to keep abreast of all the technical advances and to keep abreast of all that is happening in his area in order to be able to propose adequate solutions to the commander as regards the use of engineers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the commander of the brigade and the commander of engineering are the ones that issue and write the daily orders for the engineering company, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A daily order is an enactment of daily command. And everybody writes their own daily orders. The commander of the brigade will do that for the brigade, and the chief of engineers or commander of engineers will do it for the company that he is in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But the chief of engineering doesn't write the daily orders; the commander of the engineering company writes the daily orders, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless it has been regulated differently by the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Vagueness. I think there's some confusion on whether or not you're talking about issuing the orders or actually writing them down. This is an important distinction, and not clear from the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness also has some doubts about issue tasks and not orders. Can you pursue it along this line, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
